'''Lee Albert Rubel''' ({{Birth date|1928|12|1}} – {{Death date|1995|3|25}}) was a [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to [[Analog computer|analog computing]].<ref name=nyt>{{cite news |title= Lee A. Rubel, 66, Computer Scientist And Mathematician|author= Wolfgang Saxon|work= The New York Times|url= https://www.nytimes.com/1995/04/13/obituaries/lee-a-rubel-66-computer-scientist-and-mathematician.html|date= April 13, 1995|access-date=4 November 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite conference |title=Empty space computes: The evolution of an unconventional supercomputer  |author=Mills, J.W. |author2=Parker, M. |author3= Himebaugh, B.  |author4= Shue, C. |author5= Kopecky, B. |author6= Weileman, C. |conference=Proceedings of the 3rd conference on Computing frontiers  |pages=115–126  |year=2006 |publisher=ACM}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |title=The nature of the extended analog computer  |author=Mills, J.W. |journal=Physica D: Nonlinear Phenomena |volume=237 |number=9 |pages=1235–1256 |year=2008 |publisher=Elsevier |doi=10.1016/j.physd.2008.03.041|bibcode=2008PhyD..237.1235M }}</ref>

==Career==
Originally from [[New York (state)|New York]], he held a Doctorate of Mathematics degree from [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]], and was professor of mathematics at [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] since 1954.<ref name=gene>{{cite web |url=http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=8249 |title= Lee Albert Rubel |author= Genealogy Project |publisher= North Dakota State University and American Mathematical Society |access-date=3 November 2012}}</ref>

He wrote for several scientific publications like the ''Complex Variables and Elliptic Equations International Journal'', the ''[[Constructive Approximation]]'' mathematical journal, the ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]'', the ''Journal of Differential Equations'', the ''Journal of Approximation Theory'', the ''[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]'', the ''[[Australian Mathematical Society#Society journals|Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society]]''. He also collaborated to the ''Functional Analysis'' periodical, the ''[[Tohoku Mathematical Journal|Tohoku Mathematical]]'', the ''[[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]'', the ''Franklin Institute-engineering and Applied Mathematics'', ''[[Combinatorica]]'', ''[[Israel Journal of Mathematics]]'', and ''Journal of Theoretical Neurobiology'', among others.

He was a member of the American Mathematical Society for 43 years,<ref>{{cite journal |title= Mathematics People |journal=Notices of the AMS |volume= 42 |issue= 7 |page = 780 |url= https://www.ams.org/notices/199507/people.pdf }}</ref> which published many of his papers in the ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]''.

He died on March 25, 1995, in [[Urbana, Illinois|Urbana]], Illinois.<ref name=nyt/>
